title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools (People Ops Guide)
author: Sofia Chen
body:
Summary:
This consolidated handbook page provides a single reference for engineers and cross-functional partners about what it means to work at Redwood: our role definitions and career ladder expectations, the benefits and perks we offer, a high-level hiring and onboarding overview, and the internal tools and access patterns you will use day-to-day. Use this page as your starting point for role-specific questions and follow the links in the appendix for policies and templates.

1) Introduction
Redwood’s people-first philosophy focuses on predictable career growth, transparent compensation and benefits, and an efficient hiring and onboarding experience that helps new hires become productive quickly. People Ops owns the handbook and processes; your manager and team leads own role-specific coaching, goal-setting, and performance feedback.

2) Roles & Career Ladders (Overview)
Short intro: We maintain discipline-specific ladders with clearly documented expectations across levels (IC and manager tracks). The ladders are intentionally outcome-focused and written to guide career development conversations.

Key principles:
- Transparency: level criteria and promotion cadence are published and measurable.
- Dual ladder: IC (e.g., SWE, MLE, Data Scientist, Designer) and manager tracks (e.g., Eng Manager, Product Manager lead).
- Promotion cadence: typical minimum time-in-level is 12 months; exceptional promotions can occur sooner with documented impact.

Table: Example career ladder summary (abridged)
| Role family | Title (level) | Typical years | Core expectations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Software Engineering | SWE I (L3) | 0-2 | Delivers assigned tasks, reliable quality, basic systems knowledge |
| Software Engineering | SWE II (L4) | 2-4 | Independently owns features, writes tests, participates in design |
| Software Engineering | Senior SWE (L5) | 4-7 | Leads designs, mentors, influences cross-team technical direction |
| Software Engineering | Staff SWE (L6) | 7+ | Drives cross-product initiatives, architectural ownership, org-level influence |
| Product Management | PM I / II | 1-5 | Defines scoped product work, partners with Eng and Design |

Promotion process (high level):
1. Manager initiates a promotion packet with candidate examples against ladder criteria.
2. Peer and cross-functional feedback collected (minimum 3 reviewers).
3. Calibration panel convened quarterly; People Ops facilitates leveling decisions.
4. Compensation and equity adjustments applied at promotion close.

Development resources and mentorship:
- Every new hire receives a career ladder doc for their role family.
- Internal mentorship program connects new hires with a buddy and a career mentor for 6 months.
- Managers are expected to run monthly career conversations and track OKRs tied to growth.

3) Benefits & Perks (Summary)
Redwood provides a competitive total rewards package designed for startup-scale growth with enterprise-grade benefits. Below are the core programs and key details. For full policy documents and enrollment instructions, see the links in the appendix.

Core benefits (high level):
- Health insurance: Medical (PPO/HMO options), dental, and vision with employer premiums covering 80% of employee-only plans.
- Retirement: 401(k) with 3% employer match on first 6% contribution.
- Equity: Annual refresh grants for most full-time employees and grants at hire; vesting schedule: 4 years, 1-year cliff.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary caregiver leave, 8 weeks secondary caregiver; job-protected and paid.
- Generous paid time off: 20 days PTO + company-observed holidays + discretionary winter break (3 business days).
- Family support: Fertility & adoption assistance, backup care stipend.
- Professional development: $2,000 annual stipend per employee and quarterly learning days for training/certifications.
- Commuter & wellness: Pre-tax commuter benefits and monthly wellness stipend.

Perks and workplace programs:
- Fully-remote first policy with optional office hubs; co-working allowance for remote employees who choose office space.
- Home office stipend at hire and refresh at 24 months.
- Company offsites: annual company retreat + smaller team offsites funded by the company.
- Referral program: $3,000 standard referrer bonus (subject to policy).

Benefits administration and timelines:
- New hires enroll in benefits within 30 days of start date.
- Open enrollment window: November 1-15 each year.
- Contact People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com for benefits escalation.

4) Hiring & Interviewing Overview (Hiring Manager & Candidate Paths)
Objective: keep hiring efficient, inclusive, and high quality. The hiring process includes defined stages, standard rubrics, and a consistent candidate experience.

High-level process for most roles:
1. Requisition & approval: Hiring manager files a req in Workday with compensation band and role profile. People Ops approves budget and job posting.
2. Sourcing & screening: Recruiter conducts initial screen and coordinates with hiring manager for take-home or phone screen.
3. Interview loop: Standardized interview loop includes a coding/design exercise (when applicable), 4-6 onsites (can be virtual), and a hiring committee review for mid-senior level roles.
4. Debrief & decision: Hiring manager collects scores, runs calibration, recruiter prepares offer.
5. Offer & negotiation: Recruiter extends offer; People Ops advises on market ranges and equity.
6. Acceptance & preboarding: Recruiter shares preboarding checklist and start date logistics.

Interview guidance and inclusivity:
- Use structured rubrics for all interviewers; avoid off-the-cuff questions.
- Interview training required annually for all interviewers (unconscious bias, inclusive hiring).
- Candidate experience SLA: initial response within 3 business days; interview loop ideally completed within 3 weeks.

Offer components and approval thresholds:
- Offers include base salary, target bonus (if applicable), equity grant, and standard benefits enrollment instructions.
- Compensation approvals follow banding matrix; exceptions require People Ops and CFO sign-off.

5) New Hire Onboarding (30-60-90 roadmap and checklist)
Goal: new hires reach baseline productivity in their first 30-90 days and feel connected to peers and company mission.

Pre-boarding (before Day 1):
- Recruiter sends welcome packet, benefits enrollment window, and hardware form.
- IT creates accounts and requests SSO access via Okta on T-5 business days.

Day 1-7 (Orientation & Setup):
- Day 1: Welcome meeting with manager, People Ops orientation, and team introductions.
- IT checklist: laptop delivered, GitHub access, Slack invite, calendar sync, and MFA setup.
- Buddy assigned and 30-day onboarding goals documented.

Day 8-30 (Ramp & Contribution):
- First project assigned (small scope) with clear acceptance criteria.
- Weekly check-ins with manager and buddy.
- Role-specific training modules completed (security, data handling, codebase walk-through).

Day 31-90 (Ownership & Impact):
- Take on larger feature or cross-team task.
- Midpoint review (30-45 days) to recalibrate goals.
- 90-day success review with manager and People Ops; outcome recorded in Workday.

Onboarding checklist (short):
- Hardware delivered and registered
- Slack, Google Workspace, GitHub, Jira, and Confluence access verified
- Security training completed (within first 7 days)
- First PR merged / first customer ticket resolved (role dependent)

6) Internal Tools & Access (Who uses what, how to request)
Primary tools (with owners and purpose):
- Slack — communications (owner: IT & People Ops)
- Google Workspace — docs, calendar, email (owner: IT)
- GitHub — source control and code reviews (owner: Eng Platform)
- Jira — issue tracking and sprint boards (owner: Eng Platform)
- Confluence — internal docs and handbooks (owner: People Ops)
- Okta — SSO and account provisioning (owner: IT/Security)
- GCP / AWS accounts — cloud resources for hosted and private deployments (owner: Eng Infra)
- Datadog & Honeycomb — observability and traces (owner: Eng Platform)
- Sentry & Rollbar — error tracking (owner: Eng Platform)
- PagerDuty — on-call alerts and escalation (owner: Eng SRE)

Access request flow:
1. New hire SSO account provisioned via Okta by IT.
2. Manager submits tool access form in Confluence (link in appendix) for role-based access.
3. Access approvals: manager + tool owner. Escalations to IT security take up to 48 business hours.

Least-privilege and data access:
- Access is role-based; request only what is required for the role.
- Sensitive data (customer PII, billing) requires additional approval and Data Access Agreement signature. See Data Management policy for details.

Standard onboarding tool checklist (examples):
- GitHub: repo access for team(s) — request code owner approval
- Jira: project and board access — request via Confluence form
- Cloud consoles: IAM role assigned — short-lived tokens for contractors

7) Performance Reviews & Compensation Rhythm
Cadence and expectations:
- Performance reviews: twice yearly (mid-year calibration in June, year-end in December).
- Calibration panels: cross-functional committees review leveling and merit increases.
- Career conversations: managers run quarterly 1:1s focused on goals and career progress.

Compensation increases and equity refreshes:
- Merit increases considered at review cycles and funded based on company performance.
- Equity refresh eligibility typically reviewed annually.
- Promotions trigger compensation and equity adjustments aligned with banding policy.

8) Manager & Team Lead Responsibilities
Managers are responsible for:
- Running regular 1:1s and career conversations
- Completing promotion packets and supporting calibration
- Ensuring psychological safety and inclusive team culture
- Onboarding new hires and assigning meaningful work

Checklist for new managers (first 60 days):
- Complete manager training in People Ops learning portal
- Conduct skip-level meetings and upward feedback sessions
- Document team goals and priorities in the team playbook

9) FAQs (short)
Q: How do I request flexible work or a permanent remote arrangement?
A: Discuss with your manager; submit flexible-work request form in Confluence. Final approvals by manager + People Ops.

Q: Who do I contact if my benefits enrollment didn’t process?
A: Email people-ops@redwood.com with subject line: Benefits Enrollment — New Hire <name>.

Q: What to do if I see suspicious activity in an account?
A: Report immediately to security@redwood.com and follow the incident response runbook.

10) Appendix (links, templates, and policy pointers)
- Onboarding checklist template: /confluence/templates/onboarding-checklist
- Career ladder docs (by discipline): /confluence/careers/ladder-swe /confluence/careers/ladder-product /confluence/careers/ladder-design
- Hiring manager guide & interview rubrics: /confluence/hiring/hiring-manager-guide
- Security & data handling: /confluence/security/data-management-policy
- Benefits & payroll provider portal: benefits-provider.redwood.com (internal link)

Document ownership and update cadence:
- Owner: People Ops (Sofia Chen)
- Review cadence: annual review in Q1 and as-needed updates following policy changes.
- Suggested editors: hiring leads, Eng managers, Eng Platform, and Eng Infra.

If you have suggested edits or updates, open a Confluence edit request or reach out to people-ops@redwood.com.
